198.t: Hair mattresses and how they were cleaned
198.s: Russell asks what a hair mattress is; Emile says it is sea hair, and describes washing it in tubs and drying it in the sun.
198.q: Well, I was always learned about this, which I don't know if it's right or wrong. That's the hair that comes from the sea.

182.t: Moving from Sox's Lane, Dubin and the high-water crevasses
182.s: Tom explains his moves from Bellashad to Sox's Lane, Dubin and then across the river, floods, and playing with Johnny Gould around the Poitras crevasse.
182.q: Yeah, I was down in Sox's land then. Then we moved from there and we moved back in, at least they call it Dubin, over to the Vida. Had a little place to go back there. You know where they got that water winks? Back there. I lived back there. What did you call it? They called it, I called it, I…

646.t: Fireside stories: Brer Rabbit and the syrup barrel
646.s: Asked about stories told by the fire, she half-recalls rabbit and bear tales, the syrup barrel, and her mother telling stories at bedtime.
646.q: Jack and the poor bee, you know. Turtle and the rabbit, and the bear, and the king. Brian, what was the bear? Something goes with the bear. I don't tend to rabbit.

1051.t: Scrubbing floors and cleaning pots with brick
1051.s: Russell asks how it was made; Mrs. Henderson explains scrubbing floors and pots with the colouring and brick.
1051.ch: The Camellia band and home life
1051.q: You buy that. Don't want the rest of them. The brick you pound. The fine did you want it. That's ready. That's ready.

188.s: Asked about McCall, Foster describes a large sugar plantation on the riverfront, now changed by the levee and highway.
188.q: because the larger the other small sugar house you call them smaller but this is a refinery you know they only didn't they didn't only made the juice they dried sugar too wasn't as big a place as the Godchalk I think so you couldn't hardly recognize the woods way back there so far from the…

665.t: The September storm and her first job in the city
665.s: She came to live with her mother and worked for a pastor; a steeple blew down in the storm.
665.q: Oh, yeah. Yeah, I said call you. He gave me a peaches. Tip to him. Don't say nothing. Tell him don't say nothing. Don't talk to him.

633.t: What became of the plantation and whether city bands visited
633.s: The plantation is now overgrown and flooded; no city bands came, only their own country band.
633.q: I went down there about, about three months ago. And I hadn't been down there for years. And I hardly know the place when I got there. Growing up in weeds and grass. Not much there.

681.t: The shop becomes a party rental business
681.s: The family moved into renting china and glassware, coined 'Entertainments Furnished', and Hirsch shows old printing cuts and stationery.
681.q: And we've got different things in here, like these things that came from the store. So, this is what we, uh, this is, then we went into the rental end of it. We went into the rental end. This, this was the China where, that we used to rent. Really? That's Austrian China. That's what you call…

50.t: First memory of Jelly and the gifts he sent
50.s: At six Jelly brought her a sweater; later a rabbit and a jeweled dresser set at sixteen, which she still keeps.
50.ch: Family and early memories of Jelly
50.q: Well, I mean, when I was six years old he brought me a pink sweater with a tassel on it And bought me some high top shoes with tassels and I never have forgotten that Really? And I was, my grandmother made, my brother brought the pink sweater to me and the blue one to my sister But my grandmother…

833.t: Moving to Robinson Street and Miss Mary's kindness
833.s: He recalls where he lived and a white woman who gave him bread and clothes.
833.ch: Mente's factory, hard times and later life
833.q: i forgot the year it'd been a good while i moved from uh from third street i think no from from robinson robinson between melton mean and uh in melton mean in this street here i had a white lady named miss mary she passes here now she knows me good i live in the 1517
